work.text: He worked hard and made a number of pencil and pen sketches which formed the basis of the oil painting known as Gassed now in the War Museum.
work.lead: Henry Tonks, on Sargent at the dressing station:

source.author: Henry Tonks
source.title: Recollection of Sargent at the front
source.publisher: quoted in Evan Charteris, John Sargent (1927; Internet Archive scan)

moment.text: The British War Memorial Committee had commissioned the work from him as a way of honoring the sacrifices of World War I. The subject was based on a scene the artist actually witnessed during his visit to battlefields in France in 1918.

source.author: The Cleveland Museum of Art
source.title: Studies of a Soldier Drinking, for Gassed (recto)

matters.text: Gassed cases kept coming in, lead along in parties of about six just as Sargent has depicted them, by an orderly. They sat or lay down on the grass, there must have been several hundred, evidently suffering a great deal, chiefly I fancy from their eyes which were covered up by a piece of lint.
matters.lead: Henry Tonks, remembering the dressing station:

matters.text: Mustard gas is a persistent vesicant gas, with effects that only become apparent several hours after exposure. It attacks the skin, the eyes and the mucous membranes, causing large skin blisters, blindness, choking and vomiting.
